title: NBA Best Bets Friday: Warriors vs Spurs, Blazers vs Kings & More Picks – Action Network Picks
body:
The NBA’s season‑opening “NBA Cup” slate rolls into its second night on Friday, November 13, with a trio of marquee match‑ups that have bettors and fans alike scanning the odds for value. The Golden State Warriors travel to San Antonio to test a rejuvenated Spurs squad, while the Portland Blazers head west to face the Sacramento Kings in a clash of two teams seeking to cement early‑season identities. Alongside those contests, the Action Network’s analytics team has identified a handful of spreads, totals and player prop bets that they believe offer the best edge for the evening’s action.

Golden State arrives in San Antonio with a 1‑1 record, having split its opening games despite the lingering absence of key pieces from last season’s championship run. Stephen Curry, now back to full health, is averaging 28.4 points and 5.9 assists, while Klay Thompson’s 22.1 points per game have kept the Warriors’ offense potent. The Spurs, meanwhile, have surprised many with a 2‑0 start, largely thanks to a balanced attack anchored by veteran guard Dejounte Murray, who is averaging 19.3 points and 7.2 assists, and a defensive scheme that forces opponents into low‑percentage shots. The spread set by bookmakers favors the Spurs by 3.5 points, reflecting home‑court advantage and recent form, but the Warriors’ firepower and a favorable pace‑of‑play metric suggest the spread could be tighter than projected. Analysts point to the Warriors’ superior offensive efficiency (115.2 rating) versus the Spurs’ defensive rating (108.7) as a key factor that may allow Golden State to cover, especially if they exploit San Antonio’s slower transition game.

In the West Coast showdown, the Blazers host the Kings in what could be a pivotal test for both teams’ young cores. Portland, currently 1‑1, leans heavily on the dynamic duo of Damian Lillard and Anfernee Simons. Lillard, still adjusting to a new supporting cast, is posting 25.7 points and 8.3 assists per contest, while Simons contributes a league‑high 22.4 points off the bench. Sacramento, also 1‑1, counters with a balanced roster featuring De’Aaron Fox’s 24.5 points and Domantas Sabonis’s 12.3 points and 10.1 rebounds, giving the Kings a potent inside‑out threat. The total for this game has been set at 237.5 points, a figure that reflects the high‑scoring potential of both offenses but also the defensive lapses each team has exhibited (both allowing over 112 points per game). Betting experts suggest taking the over, citing the Kings’ 42.5% three‑point shooting rate and Portland’s recent trend of exceeding the line in five of their last seven outings.

Beyond the headline fixtures, Friday’s NBA Cup schedule includes several under‑the‑radar match‑ups that could produce profitable outcomes. The Miami Heat, playing at home against the Chicago Bulls, are favored by 5.5 points, yet the Bulls’ recent surge in defensive efficiency (ranked 8th in the league) may keep the game within a single‑digit margin, making the Bulls +5.5 a tempting pick for contrarian bettors. Meanwhile, the New York Knicks host the Detroit Pistons in a game where the total has been posted at 227 points. Pistons rookie Jaden Ivey has been exceeding his projected scoring line, and the Knicks’ inconsistent perimeter defense could push the total over the line.

In terms of player props, the consensus among analysts is to watch the emerging play‑making role of Jordan Poole for Golden State. Poole’s assists per game have risen to 4.2 this season, and a prop betting line of 4.5 assists appears undervalued given his increased minutes and the Warriors’ reliance on secondary ball‑handlers. Similarly, Sacramento’s Sabonis is projected to record a double‑double in rebounds and points, with the line set at 11.5 rebounds. Sabonis has averaged 11.8 rebounds over his last ten games, indicating a favorable edge for the over.

As the NBA Cup progresses, early‑season trends are beginning to crystallize, offering both bettors and fans clearer narratives about which teams are poised to contend and which are still searching for identity.
